about: Every stored baseline in tools/, and what it can still be used for. Written in S4 task 3.6a from a measurement at 5803067, not from memory: all 14 files re-verified with tools/capture-baseline.js verifyIntegrity() (14 clean), and each classified by the tool's own encodingOf() and completenessOf(). NOTHING HERE EDITS A BASELINE -- historical evidence stays exactly as it was captured (ground rule 9 as amended by S4-PA-03). The format gate is not widened for any of them (Q28). tests/baseline-registry.test.js holds this file to the directory, to each file's own contents, and to what diffSnapshots() actually does with each status.

statuses.historical: FORMAT 1: runScenario() output, with identity.scenarioId and identity.runId excluded. diffSnapshots() refuses to compare it with any later format, deliberately: the whole identity block would read as removed on every scenario, a fact about the entry point and not the engine. So it cannot be re-verified against a current capture, it records no corpus-input hash and no commit, and it is NOT a baseline. Kept as the record of what the engine produced when it was taken.
statuses.superseded-format: FORMAT 2: runPlan() output under the format-2 encoding. Refused for diffing against a current (format 3) capture for the same reason as format 1, and it records no completeness metadata. Comparable only with another format-2 capture, and never a verified regression pass.
statuses.current-format-completeness-unknown: FORMAT 3 without completeness metadata. Comparable with a current capture and its differences are real, but agreement with it is not a verified regression pass: the tool refuses an empty diff against it unless diagnostic comparison is asked for explicitly (P9-01).
statuses.baseline: FORMAT 3, declares itself complete with no omissions, records its corpus-input hash and commit, and verifies clean. Comparable with a current capture of the same corpus inputs; an empty diff against it is a regression pass.

provenanceAbout: S4 task 5.1 (Q37): does each file's recorded commit identify the engine that produced it? verifyIntegrity() cannot say -- meta.hash does not cover meta.gitCommit -- so this is a separate measurement. Measured 2026-09-13 on a tree whose HEAD was bf4e6d9 (the parent of the commit adding this block; a file cannot name the commit that contains it): tools/verify-baseline-provenance.js replay, in a clean clone with core.autocrlf=false, checking out each recorded commit and running THAT commit's own capture tool; and its sources check against git objects. Q37's nested-extraction defect produced none of these records. One record was captured from a dirty working tree instead, which is the gap Q37's own entry named. Classifying is not repairing: no file is edited or recaptured, and a commit found to reproduce a file is recorded here, beside it. tests/baseline-provenance.test.js holds every classification to the files and, in a checkout of this repository, to its history. Added S5AA R40 (2026-09-30): a provenance whose "repository" is "this" records a commit made in this public repository; every other recorded commit is in the private archive this repository was copied from. The two are checked apart: the archive's commits are all present or none are, and this repository's must all be present in any checkout of it.

provenanceClasses.reproduced: A clean checkout of the recorded commit, running that commit's own capture tool, writes this file byte for byte (line endings normalised). The recorded commit identifies the engine that produced it.
provenanceClasses.reproduced-output: At the recorded commit the capture reproduces every entry, meta.hash, the corpus-input hash, the source hashes and the recorded commit, but some metadata differs; differingLeaves names it. The recorded commit identifies the engine; the metadata was written by a different version of the tool.
provenanceClasses.unqualified-wrong-commit: The recorded commit does NOT reproduce this capture. HISTORICAL/UNQUALIFIED: it must not be cited as that commit's output. The file is kept exactly as captured. sourcesAtRecordedCommit says whether its source hashes match that commit's bytes; reproducesAt, when present, names a commit found to reproduce it, as a recorded fact that is never written into the file.
provenanceClasses.unqualified-no-commit: The capture records no commit (format 1). There is no provenance claim to verify, so none is made. Kept as historical.
